description: Renders the workspace's visual map to an image and returns it so you can SEE it the way the user does when they open Map: a transit-style map seen from above. Each workflow is a colored tile with a short code; people are round figures, systems are small squares with a drum, other pages are plain tiles, each named underneath. Lines along the grid join linked pages, solid between a workflow and what it touches, dashed between other pages; pages that link to each other more than to the rest gather into named regions on a pale ground plate, and pages connected to nothing sit together in a "Not connected" plate. zv1's drafts that nobody has accepted are drawn faint. Use this when the user asks about the shape of their map, where things cluster, what connects to what, or anything spatial. The text part counts the pages of each type, the links, and how many pages are unconnected, plus `mapUrl`. The image is for you to look at; do NOT put it in your reply as a markdown image (the chat can't show it). When the user should see the map, link `mapUrl` — e.g. `[Open your map](mapUrl)` — and describe what you saw.

workspace.description: Workspace slug. Personal tokens with no default workspace MUST pass this; tokens with a default can override per call. Ignored for workspace API keys.
